title: Legislative districts of Surigao del Norte
wikitext:
{{Politics of the Philippines}} The '''legislative districts of Surigao del Norte''' are the representations of the [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Surigao del Norte]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The province is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through its [[#1st District|first]] and [[#2nd District|second]] congressional districts. The 1st legislative district comprises nine municipalities on the islands of [[Siargao]] and [[Bucas Grande]] (plus smaller islands); the 2nd legislative district comprises Surigao City and eleven other municipalities on the mainland of Mindanao. == History == {{further|Legislative district of Surigao}} Prior to gaining separate representation, areas now under the jurisdiction of Surigao del Norte were represented under the former province of [[Surigao (province)|Surigao]] (1907–1961). The enactment of Republic Act No. 2786 on June 19, 1960, split the old Surigao province into [[Surigao del Norte]] and [[Surigao del Sur]], and provided the new provinces separate representations in Congress.{{cite web|title=Republic Act No. 2786 - An Act to Create the Provinces of Surigao del Norte and Surigao del Sur|date=June 19, 1960|access-date=February 7, 2016|author=Congress of the Philippines|website=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library|url=http://www.chanrobles.com/republicacts/republicactno2786.html}} The new province of Surigao del Norte first elected its [[#Lone District (defunct)|own representative]] in the [[1961 Philippine general election|1961 elections]]. Surigao del Norte was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region X]] from 1978 to 1984, and returned [[#At-Large (defunct)|one representative, elected at large]], to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]]. The province was reapportioned into [[House of Representatives of the Philippines#District representation|two congressional districts]] under the new Constitution{{cite web|title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines - Apportionment Ordinance|url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/|author=1986 Constitutional Commission|date=February 2, 1987|access-date=November 21, 2017|website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines}} which was proclaimed on February 11, 1987, and elected members to the restored House of Representatives starting [[1987 Philippine legislative election|that same year]]. The passage of Republic Act No. 9355 and its subsequent [[2006 Dinagat Islands creation plebiscite|ratification by plebiscite]] in December 2006 separated seven municipalities from Surigao del Norte's [[#1987–2007|first congressional district]] to form the new province of [[Dinagat Islands]], which began to elect its own representative in the [[2007 Philippine House of Representatives elections|2007 elections]].{{cite web|title=Republic Act No. 9355 - An Act Creating the Province of Dinagat Islands|date=October 2, 2006|access-date=August 9, 2016|author=Congress of the Philippines|website=Senate of the Philippines|url=https://www.senate.gov.ph/republic_acts/ra%209355.pdf}} Despite Dinagat Islands being nullified as a province by the [[Supreme Court of the Philippines]] on February 11, 2010{{cite news|last1=Rempillo|first1=Jay B.|title=SC Voids Creation of the Province of Dinagat Islands|url=http://sc.judiciary.gov.ph/news/courtnews%20flash/2010/02/02111002.php|access-date=December 19, 2015|publisher=Supreme Court of the Philippines|date=February 11, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110716102903/http://sc.judiciary.gov.ph/news/courtnews%20flash/2010/02/02111002.php|archive-date=July 16, 2011}} the decision was not yet rendered final and executory before the [[2010 Philippine general election|10 May 2010 elections]]; therefore the [[Commission on Elections (Philippines)|Commission on Elections]] still organized separate elections for the Dinagat Islands' [[Legislative district of Dinagat Islands|congressional representative]] and provincial officials.{{cite web|author=Commission on Elections|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100326191935/https://comelec.files.wordpress.com/2010/03/com_res_8790.pdf|archive-date=March 26, 2010|title=COMELEC Resolution No. 8790|url=https://comelec.files.wordpress.com/2010/03/com_res_8790.pdf|date=March 9, 2010|access-date=August 9, 2016|url-status=dead}} The representatives of the [[#1st District|reconfigured first district]] of Surigao del Norte and the lone district of Dinagat Islands continued to represent their respective constituencies even after the Supreme Court rendered its original decision final and executory on 18 May 2010.{{cite web|url=http://sc.judiciary.gov.ph/jurisprudence/2011/april2011/180050.htm|date=April 12, 2011|title=G.R. No. 180050 - RODOLFO G. NAVARRO, VICTOR F. BERNAL, and RENE O. MEDINA, Petitioners, - versus - EXECUTIVE SECRETARY EDUARDO ERMITA, representing the President of the Philippines; Senate of the Philippines, represented by the SENATE PRESIDENT; House of Representatives, represented by the HOUSE SPEAKER; GOVERNOR ROBERT ACE S. BARBERS, representing the mother province of Surigao del Norte; GOVERNOR GERALDINE ECLEO VILLAROMAN, representing the new Province of Dinagat Islands, Respondents|publisher=Supreme Court of the Philippines|first=Antonio Eduardo B.|last=Nachura|access-date=August 9, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160819044441/http://sc.judiciary.gov.ph/jurisprudence/2011/april2011/180050.htm|archive-date=August 19, 2016|url-status=dead}} After the Supreme Court reversed its previous ruling on April 12, 2011, and subsequently upheld with finality the constitutionality of Republic Act No. 9355 and the creation of Dinagat Islands as a province through an Entry of Judgment on October 24, 2012,{{cite web|url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/2013/01/09/ira-shares-for-lgus-jump-by-37-5-in-2013/|title=IRA Shares for LGUs Jump by 37.5% in 2013|date=January 9, 2013|publisher=Office of the President of the Philippines|author=Department of Budget and Management|website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines|access-date=August 9, 2016}} the separation of Dinagat Islands from Surigao del Norte's first district became permanent. == Current districts == {{Color box|{{party color|Lakas-Christian Muslim Democrats}}|border=darkgray}} [[Lakas–CMD]] (1)
